title: Man was 'little bit fidgety,' friend tells Taser inquest
article: A coroner's inquest into the death of a 25-year-old man minutes after he was Tasered by police heard conflicting stories Monday about what happened in the moments before he was shocked.
Roman Andreichikov had been on a five-day crack binge and had twice tried to commit suicide by throwing himself off his balcony when his friend, Rahim Hadani, called 911 on May 1, 2004.
Testifying by phone from Toronto, Hadani told the inquest Monday he asked for an ambulance but police were the first on the scene.
As the police walked through the door, said Hadani, one of the officers already had his Taser out.
Hadani said Andreichikov had earlier been pacing around his apartment and scratching himself, but he was sitting on his couch rocking back and forth when police came in.
"He was a little bit fidgety, that's about it," said Hadani.
None of the officers who responded to the incident have testified yet, but some of their earlier statements were read out by lawyers Monday.
Those statements described Andreichikov "screaming at the top of his lungs," walking back and forth and acting like a "caged wild animal."
The officers also said they had to ask Andreichikov several times to lie face down, while Hadani said he lay down when asked the first time.
According to one of the officer's statements, Andreichikov then jumped up and looked as if he might lunge at police.
Hadani said Andreichikov merely tried to roll over.
It was at that moment that Const. Darren Hall shot his Taser.
After Andreichikov was shocked, said Hadani, the four officers began holding him down -- including one who had his entire weight on his back.
Hadani said Andreichikov was screaming in pain and struggled with police for a few minutes.
Hadani testified he heard Andreichikov mumble several times that he couldn't breathe.
"The guy that was sitting on top of him said: 'If you're mumbling, you're breathing,' " said Hadani.
A few moments later, said Hadani, Andreichikov's body went completely limp.
He was confirmed dead a few minutes later.
Kevin Woodall, who is representing Hall at the hearing, challenged Hadani's recollection and read from a transcript of an interview Hadani gave to police the night of Andreichikov's death.
"Somebody asked if he was breathing still and somebody said: 'Well, yeah, he's mumbling, so he must be breathing,' " Hadani said in the statement.
That statement, said Woodall, suggests the officer's statement was in response to an inquiry from another officer -- not Andreichikov.
Hadani said he was stressed out the night of the incident and that his recollection Monday was the more accurate one.
The inquest also heard from Andreichikov's girlfriend, Jaimie Layno, who had a fight with him the day of his death.
Layno said Andreichikov had been smoking crack for days and was becoming increasingly paranoid, including falsely accusing her of being in a porn film.

Outside the hearing room, Andreichikov's mother Diana Andreichikov said she didn't think it was necessary for police to Taser her son. "He wasn't dangerous to anybody," she said. "He had no knife, no gun, nothing."
Lawyer Phil Rankin, who is representing the family at the inquest, said he thinks police should have tried others means of calming Andreichikov down.
"I'm trying to find out of it they could have controlled him without a Taser," he said.
The inquest continues today.
